LONDON, England (CNN) -- Deep into injury time in one of Manchester United's most important games of the English Premier League season a 17-year-old Italian on debut hit a stunning winner and lifted himself to instant stardom. Man of the moment: Seventeen-year-old Federico Macheda is now a legend at Manchester United . Federico Macheda was the teenager who came on as a substitute and scored late on Sunday for the Red Devils -- helping them to a 3-2 win after they had earlier trailed 2-1 to Aston Villa at Old Trafford. The finish was of the highest quality -- as he curled the ball past Villa goal-keeper Brad Freidel from a wide angle. His fine touch, turn and shot were made all the more amazing given their significance in the context of both the match and season. But, who is this 17-year-old hero? And how did he get to live his fairytale? Born in Rome in 1991 (yes, 1991), Macheda, known by team-mates as "Kiko", is a striker who developed his game through the ranks of the Lazio youth programme in Italy -- where he is considered as one of the brightest talents of the future. He made a move to Manchester United in September 2007, and quickly moved up the ranks -- starting out in the under-18 side, before progressing to the senior reserve team. He officially signed a professional contract with the club on his 17th birthday, in August 2008. Although Sunday's goal puts his name permanently on the minds of all Manchester United faithful, it's not the first time he has made an impression. Just six days before he scored a thrilling hat-trick for the reserve team in a 3-3 draw against Newcastle at St James' Park. He has also represented Italy at under 19 level. What did you think of Macheda's goal? Can he go on to become a top club and international player? Share your thoughts in the Sound Off box below. Macheda was eventually booked for celebrating with the crowd after his strike -- though he later revealed he had hugged family members -- who were in the crowd to see his debut. He was named man of the match for his goal (after playing just 30 minutes) and although he wasn't allowed the bottle of wine he won for the honor -- he told Manchester United television "this is the best day of my life." In the post-match interview on Sky Sports, Macheda said: "I think this is the day of my dreams -- to score a goal like that on my debut." The Manchester United Supporters' Web site has since been inundated with comments praising Macheda, and there are even several proposed supporters' chants being drafted for their new star. English-based Italian football journalist Gabriele Marcotti told CNN he had been impressed by Macheda's progress at a young age -- but felt it was important he didn't get ahead of himself. "When a guy scores like that on debut there's always excitement. But, he needs to keep his feet on the ground and keep working," Marcotti said. Marcotti said the reaction from Italian fans was likely to be mixed. While there would be happiness that he is emerging as a great prospect for Italy in future, there is also concern that players like Macheda are moving to England at a young age and the Italian clubs who train them gain very little in compensation, he said.

# Teenager Macheda fires Manchester United back to the summit

**MANCHESTER, England (CNN) —** Federico Macheda was barely known outside Manchester United’s training ground before Sunday. One inspired turn and curling shot later, the 17-year-old Italian had become the unlikely hero of the Premier League title race.

Macheda came off the bench to score an injury-time winner as United defeated Aston Villa 3-2 at Old Trafford, sending the defending champions back above Liverpool at the top of the table.

With the match level at 2-2 and United’s title challenge appearing to falter, Macheda collected Ryan Giggs’ pass, turned Villa defender Luke Young and guided a right-footed shot beyond goalkeeper Brad Friedel and inside the far post.

“I turned and shot and the ball went in,” Macheda told reporters after his first-team debut. “It was the best day of my life.”

The goal sparked an eruption inside Old Trafford. Supporters surged to their feet, while Macheda raced toward the crowd before disappearing beneath a pile of red shirts. United manager Alex Ferguson celebrated on the touchline as his side completed a dramatic recovery.

“The audacity to try that was fantastic,” Ferguson said of the finish.

## From Rome to Manchester

Born in Rome on August 22, 1991, Macheda began his football education with Lazio. But Italian regulations prevented the Serie A club from tying him to a professional contract before his 18th birthday.

United took advantage, bringing the forward and his family to England in 2007 when he was 16.

Known as “Kiko” to teammates, Macheda progressed through United’s academy and reserve sides. His elevation to the first-team squad followed a hat-trick for the reserves against Newcastle earlier in the week.

Ferguson turned to the teenager with United trailing 2-1 and missing several established attackers. Cristiano Ronaldo had scored the opening goal, but John Carew and Gabriel Agbonlahor put Villa ahead. Ronaldo equalized in the 80th minute before Macheda delivered the decisive moment deep into stoppage time.

## An instant Old Trafford favorite

The teenager’s name echoed around the stadium after the final whistle, with supporters lingering to celebrate a player many had not expected even to see on the field.

Fan forums and message boards quickly filled with tributes, while television replays of the goal showed Macheda’s family celebrating in the stands. For United supporters, the finish invited memories of the club’s long tradition of academy players making an immediate impact.

Yet Ferguson sought to temper the excitement surrounding his new forward, stressing that one goal did not guarantee a lasting career at the highest level.

The manager nevertheless acknowledged that Macheda’s composure had been exceptional for a player making his debut in such a pressured situation.

## Italy’s teenage departures

Macheda’s move also renewed debate in Italy about the loss of young players to English clubs.

Under Football Association rules, English teams can offer professional terms to players at 17. In Italy, clubs cannot sign players to full professional contracts until they are 18, leaving leading academies vulnerable to approaches from abroad.

Macheda followed a path already taken by fellow Italians Giuseppe Rossi, who joined United from Parma, and Arturo Lupoli, who left Parma for Arsenal. Both moves prompted concern among Italian clubs that Premier League teams could recruit promising teenagers before their home clubs were able to secure them.

For the players, England can offer modern training facilities, reserve-team competition and — in rare cases — an early opportunity on one of football’s biggest stages. The risks are equally clear: separation from home, intense competition and no guarantee of first-team football.

On Sunday, however, Macheda’s decision appeared fully justified.

In the space of a few seconds, the teenager from Rome had gone from reserve-team prospect to Old Trafford hero — and may have changed the course of the Premier League title race.
